newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria wants to start EU talks early.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria wants to start EU talks early.

text.p: Bulgaria, one of the candidate states set to be left out of the next wave of European Union expansion, said on Monday that all ex-communist countries should be allowed to start EU membership negotiations together.

Such a move by the EU "would be a confirmation that all countries have equal chances to become members of a united Europe", a government statement said, adding that each would actually join the EU only when it was ready.
The European Commission last week invited Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Estonia and Slovenia to begin talks next year on joining the EU.

But it rejected applications from Bulgaria, Romania, Lithuania, Latvia and Slovakia, instead pledging to design a pre-accession strategy to help them carry out necessary reforms and promising to review their progress each year.

Bulgaria admitted that in several years of reform communist government it had fallen behind other East European states in introducing a market economy and land reform and in developing the private sector.
The statement said Bulgaria's new conservative government appreciated the faith expressed by the European Commission that it would now quickly get on with reform.
The government of the Union of Democratic Forces took office in May after the Socialist Party was forced out by mass protests.
The commission says Bulgaria is on its way to satisfying the political criteria for EU membership.
But its says Bulgaria must commit itself to market reform to get out of an economic crisis. Last year the economy shrank 10.9 percent, public deficits ballooned and inflation hit 311 percent.
